projects.name: NeoWorks
projects.tagline: Your photos, calendar and contacts, kept to yourself.
projects.description: NeoWorks is my company. It stores and syncs personal data that is encrypted on your device before it ever leaves it. Photos, calendars and contacts run on it, and other apps can build on the same storage through the SDK.
features: End-to-end encrypted storage and sync: data is encrypted on your device
Photos, calendar and contacts apps on the web and on Android
An SDK and OAuth so third-party apps can store data on NeoWorks
One shared crypto core in C++, compiled to WebAssembly for the browser
Start free with 1 GB

projects.name: Gyro
projects.tagline: A systems language that refuses the program when it is wrong.
projects.description: A systems language with manual memory and explicit effects, built so that a machine can generate code in it and be caught when it is wrong. Gyro compiles to the METALS IR, a shared intermediate representation that several languages lower into, and from there to native Linux x86-64 binaries.
projects.code: import { println, Array } from "stdlib" import { heap } from "mem" export struct Stack { export capacity: i32 items: Array<i32> } // A slice borrows, so the row names where the view came from. // Without `&self` this does not compile. export fn Stack::view(self): i32[] !{ &self } { return self.items.slice() } fn main() { var stack = Stack::new(16) defer stack.free() stack.push(2) stack.push(40) println("total: #{total(stack.view())}") }
features: No zero values, no implicit conversions, overflow that panics instead of wrapping
Effect rows like !{ io } and borrow provenance written into signatures
Manual memory over explicit allocators, with defer and leak warnings
Exhaustive matches, traits, generics, channels and async / await
Imports C headers and .c files directly through the METALS IR
Compiles to native Linux x86-64 binaries

projects.name: Otter
projects.tagline: Find something to watch. Press play. That's it.
projects.description: Movies and series from all over the web in one cozy place. Search any film or show, Otter finds where it streams and lets you watch right away. It runs on your home server or NAS and on your Android phone, so your library, watchlist and progress are always with you.
features: Search every movie and series, with posters, trailers, cast and ratings
Checks many streaming sites at once and lists every source it finds
Recommendations that learn from what you watch, rate and save
Watch history, progress and a watchlist for every profile
Offline downloads, casting to the TV and Watch Together rooms on Android
New streaming sites plug in as small JavaScript plugins

projects.name: Drift
projects.description: A YouTube Music player for desktop and Android without a server in between: every app talks to YouTube Music directly through one shared Go core. Anonymous by default, and your Spotify or YouTube Music library comes along with one import.
features: Plays all of YouTube Music, no account needed
Imports your library from Spotify or YouTube Music
Synced lyrics, offline downloads and podcasts
Recommendations and a magic shuffle that run on your device, no ML and no account
Listen Together rooms with friends over WebRTC

projects.name: Latent
projects.tagline: A raw photo editor, because Lightroom doesn't run on Linux.
projects.description: I shoot a lot of photos and edit them on Linux, so I'm building my own editor. A C++ engine renders on the GPU, every edit is a step on a stack, and instead of pushing sliders you can also just tell an agent what to change. Still early.
features: Raw development on the GPU, every edit a step you can undo
Masks that pick out a person or the sky on their own
A library with folders, collections, ratings and flags
Agents edit through MCP, and a Python console uses the same API
Open source, Linux only for now
